LAREDO, Texas — South Laredo’s District 1 council seat is on the Nov. 3 ballot, and the race pits a sitting council member against a challenger who has stayed out of the spotlight — so far, according to KGNS.

Incumbent Gilbert Gonzalez, who took office nearly four years ago, is seeking another term representing South Laredo. Before joining the council, Gonzalez spent almost three decades working for South Laredo’s justice of the peace and commissioner’s court, where he ran youth programs.

Gonzalez told KGNS his early priorities were the unglamorous basics: aging water lines, weekend gunfire and unpaved roads. On water, he said the city brought in outside engineers and pressed state and federal leaders for funding to fix the problems. On crime, he pointed to new gunshot-detection technology he says is helping police respond in South Laredo neighborhoods.

Looking ahead, Gonzalez said he would take a cautious approach to data centers, arguing the city is not prepared when it comes to water and electricity capacity — and he invoked the memory of 2021 as a warning. On police surveillance cameras, he acknowledged a generational split among his constituents: residents 35 and older say the cameras make them feel safer, while younger residents have other concerns.

Challenger Lupe De Leon Jr. could not be reached for comment, KGNS reported.

District 1 is one of four council seats up for election this cycle, alongside the mayor’s race and Municipal Court Judge Place 1. Early voting runs through Oct. 30.

Sources: KGNS reporting (Oct. 22, 2026).

excerpt: District 1 voters will choose between incumbent Gilbert Gonzalez — touting water-line fixes and gunshot-detection tech — and challenger Lupe De Leon Jr., who couldn't be reached for comment.
title: District 1 council race: Gonzalez seeks another term against De Leon
